stories.title: Why Apple’s camera-equipped AirPods may not be the ‘pervert pods’ consumers fear
stories.simple_summary: Apple is designing camera earbuds that won't let people secretly record photos or videos. This design choice is meant to protect people's privacy.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're worried about people secretly recording you in public or at your business, this shows Apple is trying to build safety into the product from the start — though these earbuds haven't been released yet.

stories.title: Warp’s new system is an out-of-the-box software factory for AI development
stories.simple_summary: A company called Warp made a new tool to help programmers build AI software more easily. It's designed to speed up the process of creating AI applications.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to software engineers and tech companies — nothing you need to act on as a small business owner.

stories.title: OpenAI launches a safer ChatGPT for teens — years after teens started using it
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI created a special version of ChatGPT designed for teenagers with extra safety features and parental controls to prevent misuse and harmful content.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have teenagers or young employees, this gives you a safer AI tool to let them use for learning.

stories.title: Perplexity’s free AI offer left it with millions more users in India
stories.simple_summary: An AI search tool called Perplexity offered free access in India for a limited time, and even after that ended, the company kept millions of new users and their revenue grew.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors watching Perplexity's business growth — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Firefox’s Smart Window promises a better AI browser
stories.simple_summary: Mozilla's Firefox web browser added AI chat that can look up current information on the internet and show you where it found the information.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Firefox, you now have access to AI help that's connected to the live web, which is more useful than AI that only knows old information.

stories.title: Google’s Pet Memory forgot who my cats are
stories.simple_summary: Google's new Pet Memory feature for smart homes is supposed to help you track your pets through cameras, but it sometimes forgets or misidentifies your animals.
stories.why_it_matters: If you were considering using this feature to monitor pets at home or at a business, know that it's still making mistakes with recognizing individual animals.

stories.title: Elon Musk broke the FAA — Palantir is picking up the pieces
stories.simple_summary: An air traffic control center in Minneapolis lost radar and communications for two hours, disrupting over 1,100 flights. A data company called Palantir is now helping fix these kinds of problems.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that critical systems like air traffic control have serious problems — unless you work in aviation, this mostly affects your travel plans if outages happen.

stories.title: ChatGPT is getting a dedicated mode for teens
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is launching a special ChatGPT mode for teenagers that combines safety features and protections to keep them from harmful content and cheating.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have teenagers or manage young employees, this gives you a safer way to let them use AI for learning and work.

stories.title: Apple’s camera-equipped AirPods appear in leaked video
stories.simple_summary: Apple is working on camera-equipped AirPods earbuds that can identify things like book covers using AI called Visual Intelligence.
stories.why_it_matters: These earbuds haven't been released yet and they're still in development — wait to see what they actually do before deciding if they matter to you.

stories.title: Anthropic’s annualized revenue surges to $65B
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic, a company that makes AI software, is making a lot of money very quickly — their yearly earnings jumped by $18 billion in just two months.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — it shows the AI business is growing fast, but it doesn't directly affect how you use AI.

stories.title: AI automation startup Relay shuts down, staff joins Google’s Chrome team
stories.simple_summary: A startup called Relay that automated tasks with AI is closing down, and its team is moving to work on AI tools inside Google's Chrome browser.
stories.why_it_matters: If you were using Relay for your business, you'll need to find a different tool, but the team's work will continue at Google.

stories.title: Amazon, which started off selling books, is destroying rare texts to train AI
stories.simple_summary: Amazon is destroying rare and valuable old books to use them for training AI systems, because these books contain unique information not found online.
stories.why_it_matters: This is concerning because irreplaceable books are being destroyed — if you care about preserving rare texts, this shows AI training can come at a cost to history and culture.
